newsitem.title: UK: BT shares jump 6 pct on light budget hit.
newsitem.headline: BT shares jump 6 pct on light budget hit.

text.p: Shares in British Telecommunications Plc spiked up by more than six percent to a record high on Thursday after escaping harsher measures in the government's budget, traders said.
By 0830 GMT, BT was up 24p at 481-1/2p after eclipsing its previous high of 484p and hitting 490p. Volume topped 14 million to rank it the second most heavily traded stock.
"They seem to have got off lightly," one trader said.
Analysts said the Labour budget announced on Wednesday should help lift Bt's UK earnings by 1.5 to 2.0 percent, excluding changes to pension fund tax credits.

A windfall earnings tax burden of around 500 million pounds was also spread out in two instalments over two years, easing the burden. BT also gains about 65 million pounds per year from a two percentage point reduction in the corporation tax rate to 31 percent, analysts said.
BT Chairman Iain Vallance said he was disappointed in being caught up in the windfall levy but recognised its burden was "considerably lower than earlier speculation might have suggested."
